svg.title: Proof. Conditional on a hit count the true label count is binomial; CP coverage remains valid after averaging over that random count. Monotonic endpoints and |K −f K| ≤kf make the envelope contain the true count’s interval on every corrupted transcript. Total hits are binomial with parameter w0ηc. A union bound proves coverage; independence of the three intervals is unnecessary. CP coverage itself follows by binomial-tail inversion, each excluded tail having probability at most β/2. Thus this is finite-sample coverage for each fixed underlying state, not a posterior probability on a parameter. □ Hits alone identify wηc, not its factors. Without efficiency information the safe bound w ≥IL ω still follows from ηc ≤1. One event constrains the source for every reader, allowing subsequent reader or sign-orientation choice without another source-confidence penalty. A transverse interval straddling zero does not become a positive-direction certificate merely by clipping its lower endpoint.
